dialogue:
Person1: Morning Person2
Person2: Morning Person1, how goes it?
Person1: Good thanks. I just wanted to ask you if you are likely to need me this week as I was thinking about going to see my parents in York. It doesn't matter which day it is but I wouldn't be available for two days.
Person2: Hmmn. Well I might have something to do on Wednesday afternoon for you, but it couold be done Thursday. Until then, it would be OK if you went off for a couple of days. If you can be on the phone at least?
Person1: No problem with phone calls. I will leave right away then.
Person2: Will you be taking the train, or?
Person1: I will probably drive it. It's already after rush hour and the advantage is if I take my car I can ferry them around a bit.
Person2: They don't have a car?
Person1: They sold it. My dad stopped driving after his stroke and my Mum finds that these days she is just too nervous to drive.
Person2: That's not unusual, as we get older. How old are your folks now, Person1?
Person1: Dad's turning 70 this year, Mum's 67. 
Person2: Well, that's not that old, really. But anyway I imagine that running a car on a pension is pointless when you have free bus passes and that.
Person1: Yes, but they do feel the lack of it when it comes to going to the garden centre and bringing back trees to plant or bags of soil.
Person2: yes, that's true
Person1: and that's what I'll be doing with them, improving the old garden a bit. 
Person2: OK. Well, give them my regards.
Person1: Will do, thanks.
summary: Person1 will leave for two days to his parents in York, to help them improve their old garden. Person2 is okay with Person1 coming back on Thursday but needs him on the phone. Person1's parents sold the car, so he will drive there and ferry them around a bit.

dialogue:
Person1: Hello Birgit! Many thanks you the NY greetings. What was 2018 like for you then? 
Person2: It has not been a good year for injuries, I'm afraid.
Person2: My bad back (bulging disc) I have had for 30 years now, and I manage it pretty well most of the time. As long as I keep fairly fit (especially my “core” muscles), it is not a big problem, as long as I don’t stand or walk slowly! I can run, walk fast, cycle, kayak, swim anything really, and all of these activities are good for me, but standing still is a real trial.
Person1: How can you manage everyday life without standing?!
Person2: Most of the time I can avoid standing, and have no problems at all, but it makes visiting art galleries and museums, and parties, a lot more difficult.
Person1: One can give museums a miss, but not parties. How about carrying one of these portable folding chairs with you?
Person2: Got one! But I feel silly with it.
Person2: This year I pushed to get a proper diagnosis of a hip which has been giving me problems on and off for 3 years. It proves to be in need of replacement..
Person1: You mentioned that at Robert's do. When do you intend to have it done?
Person2: Not sure but I did a lot of phoning round of friends in the medical profession (doctors, surgeons, physios, nurses etc – 14 of them). With one exception they all said to leave it as long as possible. I also spoke to about 11 friends who had had the operation. Every one of them said it was the best thing they had ever done, and to book it in as soon as possible! So that was really helpful!
Person1: Don't you have one surgeon with an overview of your bones' condition? I've got one myself since the first symptoms of arthritis.
Person2: My GP said exercise as much as you can, and if it hurts, keep taking the painkillers! So at the moment that is what I am doing. I have decided to give it a year, and see how the land lies then.
Person1: Sounds sensible. I refused that my knee be operated on 2 years ago and I'm still going strong.
Person2: Exactly! They operate much too often. As long as I can practise sport and have my activities filled holidays I won't get under their knives.
Person1: <file_photo> It's me in the gym the other day. Talking about operations...
Person2: My point exactly!
Person2: <file_photo> And me on a cycling tour in Morocco earlier this year. We shouldn't complain!
Person1: Chins up!
summary: Person2 has problems with her back and her hip. She thinks about operation and talked about it with doctors and friends, who know the problem. However, she's not going to have her body operated, until she can't practice sports and other activities.

Took my breath away for a sec. I even yelled or groaned or gasped. Anyway I was on the floor, shocked. Absolutely shocked. I thought, so that's how it happens. But I managed to get up and didn't realise the pain until I stretched to put my nighty on. Oh bro... Horrible....

Person2: Can you touch your bruised side? Is it swollen? Red?
Person1: I can touch it, not press of course, but stroke. No, it isn't swollen. The skin is as usual, no discolouration. But this will come later, I suppose.
Person2: Not necessarily. It might as well remain unaffected. I mean the epidermis, the skin itself. Though I'd expect it to develop a bruise.
Person2: Are you coughing? Coughing blood?
Person1: God! No! I'll see how I feel in the morning. I just need a rest. I feel so rotten, bro...
Person2: My worry would be that you've damaged something inside you. You know, split spleen, punctured lung.That sort of thing.You just watch your body.
Person1: Yes, I will. I understand what you mean. I thought so as well. Just see how I feel tomorrow morning. Fucking hell! I can hardly pull myself up.
Person2: If I were you, I would go and see the doc first thing in the morning.
Person1: And he'll send me to have an x-ray. I can't bear the thought of driving or even walking.
Person2: Well, he can come to your place and you'll be driven to hospital in an ambulance.
Person1: You stop scaring the shit out of me! I am not that invalid. It's just bloody painful but I think I'm in one piece.
Person2: I don't know Person1. One shouldn't take it too light those falls. You may still be in a state of shock and are underrating your condition. Will you phone me first thing in the morning please? Still from bed? Luise is gone by 7:30, so you won't be waking anyone up.
Person1: OK brother. I will give you a call. Of course if I'm still alive.
Person2: Sister!! Anyway I wish you a good night's sleep. Have a good rest!
Person1: Thanks bro. Sleep tight too. 
Person1: And don't worry about me.

dialogue:
Person1: Hello my dear friends, we hope you are fine. We are missing you every day.

And that for a simple reason that airbnb doesn't list anything sensible and we didn't want to risk walking around the town dragging our suitcases and ask around for a room to rent. This hotel is just an easy option for us. It is quite OK, a bit too expensive, but in fact quite comfortable.

Person2: It's only breakfast as we prefer to eat in town. Every day a new place! Trinidad is absolutely fantastic for food with its choice of nearly a 100 restaurants. Pity so many of them are definitely too expensive for us. They are so beautiful!
Person1: Sorry to hear that. But a fancy interior doesn't mean necessarily good food, does it?
Person2: Not at all. We are absolutely happy with the place we've visited so far. The food was always excellent and the decor interesting. Very atmospheric places!
Person1: Glad to hear it. I wish you only good experiences for the rest of your stay in Cuba.

Person1: Pleasure.
summary: Person2 stayed at Person1's place Casa Leo in Cuba. Both wrote positive reviews of the stay on airbnb. In Trinidad Person2 decided to stay in Las Cuevas, a state-run hotel. It was comfortable, but a bit expensive.

summary: Person1's husband is back home after doing the biopsy. They will contact the urologist in 10 days. Person1 says that it's too early for alternative therapies. His husband will have eyes surgery.

dialogue:
Person1: Hi Person2
Person2: Oh, hi Fran
Person1: I guess you're as horrified by tomorrow's exam as I am
Person2: I guess so too

Person2: It's easy actually, plus there is a good Wikipedia page about them XD
Person1: I trust your notes from class more than Wiki
Person2: And rightly so! Anyway
Person1: I'm listening (or rather reading)
Person2: A substratum or substrate is essentially a language that existed in a given territory before another language
Person1: Ok
Person2: Then people speaking a different language arrived in that territory and slowly their language became the dominant one
Person1: And then the older language influences the new one, right?
Person2: Yes. The substratum slowly disappears but leaves some traces in the new language (the superstratum) like some words, pronunciation aspects and so on
Person1: Ok, so for example the Etruscan language was the substratum and Latin the superstratum, right?
Person2: Yes, and Etruscan influenced the local variety of latin in later centuries
Person1: Ok
Person2: I have a question too
Person1: You? I thought you were Mr. Perfect Notes
Person2: I am, but I missed two lessons in November
Person1: Ok
Person2: So... what was exactly the story with the name "Mediolanum"?
Person1: Ok, I know this one. In the ancient Celtic languages the Indoeuropean consonant "p" wasn't pronounced, for example the word for "father" was "athir" (vs. "pater" in Latin for example). So according to many scholars "Mediolanum" came from "medio-" and "planum" because there is no "p", so it's basically "in the middle of the plane".
Person2: Ok! Thanks
Person1: You're more than welcome, you helped me too
Person2: ;)
Person1: Good luck for tomorrow!
Person2: Godspeed!
summary: Person1 and Person2 are worrying about their exam tomorrow. Person1 uses Person2's notes. Person2 explains the notions of substrata, superstrata, and Mediolanum to her.

Person2: It really feels like a new journey, so excited! :)
Person1: You need to come over so I can show you some recipes! And remember - if you have any doubts, problems, you can always ask me, I'll do my best to help :)

summary: Person2 is working with the AIESEC. Person1 is interested in AIESEC's projects in Asia and Northern America. dialogue:
Person1: Only 1 month till Christmas!
Person2: Yeah, time's really flying, isn't it?
Person1: Tell me about it. I still remember last Christmas as if it was yesterday.
Person2: Who usually buys the gifts in your family.
Person1: Ronnie loves buying presents for the kids. He usually picks them out so meticulously.
Person2: I do all the buying in my family. Hank's usually busy with work at this time of year. It's so interesting to see how shopping's moved to the net over the years.
Person1: I know. I remember like 10 years ago, no one would have thought twice about choosing clothes by just looking at the pics online.
Person2: Toys are a little easier. I mean, obviously there's no difference between the toy at the store and the one on your screen. Plus, you can do your shopping in pajamas!
Person1: True. But it's kind of sad how everything changed in the last 10 years. It's such a short span of time. There's just something about shopping around the holidays, there's a certain magic in the air, you know what I mean?
Person2: I hear ya. But I thought Ronnie does all the Christmas shopping :)
Person1: He does, but you obviously I have to pick out his gift :)
Person2: Speaking of Ronnie, what are you planning for him this year?
Person1: Well, I was thinking of a nice watch? What do you think?
Person2: I'm sure he'll love it. I'm buying my beau a new toolkit. He's been kind of hinting at it for a long while. Where are you guys going for Christmas this year?
Person1: We're going to Hank's for Christmas Eve and then we're going to my family the next day. A marathon, like usual!
Person2: That's the thing about the holidays, you wait for them, but then you're glad their over :)
Person1: I just hope it snows this year. It seems like it's been a while since we've had snow in Dec.
Person2: I don't mind not having any, actually. It makes driving so much easier, you know.
Person1: I usually drive more than you during Christmas ;) Your family is all in one city!
Person2: Yeah, but you wouldn't believe the traffic in the city. Once you leave out on the highway, you leave all the traffic behind. Speaking of traffic, I'm stuck in it now. Actually, I shouldn't be texting you now. I gotta watch it for cops
Person1: Ok, talk to you later.
Person2: Ok, bye
summary: Person2 and Person1 are surprised how Christmas shopping has changed over the past 10 years, although Ronnie does most of the shopping for Person1. Person2 has to do it herself. Person1 has to drive a lot during Christmas, while Person2 stays in the city.

dialogue:
Person1: Hello, I did shopping in your store today and I believe there is a problem.
Person2: Good morning, what happened?
Person1: I think I’ve been charged twice for one of the products.
Person2: I see. The procedure is has a few steps, I’ll present them to you one by one.
Person1: Ok, go on.
Person2: First, you need to send us a copy of the receipt, you can do this online, detailed instructions are on our website.
Person1: Of course, what’s the second step?
Person2: More complicated, it requires you to show up in our store.
Person1: When?
Person2: We process your application in 5 business days and then a manager will contact you to organize the meeting.
Person1: Will he call me or send me an e-mail?
Person2: We prefer calling, as it is easier to communicate and go through all details. You can choose your preferred way of communication and set up the times you’re most usual available to talk.
Person1: That’s ok, I just don’t check my e-mail so often, that’s why I’m asking.
Person2: No problem, as I said the form of communication is up to you, don’t forget about it while sending your application.
Person1: It will be somewhere in the options?
Person2: Yes, all the steps are explained in details on our website.
Person1: Great, so how does the meeting look like?
Person2: While processing your application we will check the video footage from the shop, trying to find out how many products you bought.
Person1: I understand, but why am I needed?
Person2: If it’s confirmed, just to sign the documents.
Person1: And if it’s not?
Person2: Then the manager will explain you further steps.
Person1: If you don’t agree, will it go to the court?
Person2: As the last instance, yes, it may happen. But we always try to resolve it in a different way.
Person1: Okay then, thank you very much for help.
summary: Person1 believes he was charged twice for one of the products when he did shopping. He has to send them a copy of the receipt first. Then he needs to show up in the store. They will check the video footage to confirm the problem.

dialogue:
Person1: Happy New Year! How's life? Any more travelling? Do you still see a lot of your travelling companion (I don’t think you ever mentioned his name). Or are you taking it easy in your rural idyll.
Person2: Hello my dear Person1! Happy New Year to you too! Am in Cuba at the moment. What a country!
Person1: Never been there myself but it's on my itinerary. What's it like?
Person2: A bit tough, truth to tell, but you'd like it. Abject living conditions for local people but we're in a "touristy" cocoon, so one easily overlooks the other side. Splendid landscapes, incredible architecture but in a more than sorry state of preservation. I love and hate to be here at the same time.
Person1: So you aren't travelling alone, I presume.
Person2: No, my travelling companion takes me along, so to speak, to his winter quarters, since his health doesn't cope that well with European winters. I couldn't afford these travels entirely on my own of course.
Person1: Always thought Cuba is not expensive. Especially the post-Fidel Cuba.
Person2: Just the contrary. In the good old days when it was supported by the Soviet Union, the living standard was not bad and they didn't have to rely on income from tourism. Then it all went down the drain, even famine and food rationing have become their daily thing. Since early 00s most not rationed goods are available only for CUC, their convertible currency. The bottom line being that whatever you buy as a tourist, you pay +/- western prices.
Person1: So how much do you two spend daily?
Person2: Staying in private houses about at least 100€, including food, transport and entrance fees. These days we are compelled to stay at a state-run Hotel and pay thru the nose - 130€ a night. No, Cuba is not cheap. But Havana Club YES.

dialogue:
Person1: We almost got scammed in Bangkok!!
Person2: What happened???
Person2: Is everything ok??
Person1: Yes, all is good. We got our money back.
Person1: So we got approached by a "friendly" stranger on the street who presented himself as a teacher and built our trust by telling family stories.
Person1: Then he recommended us some tourists attractions i.e. The Happy Buddha and some "excellent" tailors, where they had the "last day of promotion" he stopped a tuktuk for us and verified the driver's license (another trick to build our trust).
Person1: The tuktuk took us to the happy Buddha. 
Person1: When we entered the temple we were approached by a very friendly "Buddhist prayer".
Person1: He said that he worked in London for the Thai trade mission.
Person1: He asked us what were our plans for the day and recommended that we went to the tailors showing us a few pictures of clothing that he "ordered" there for him and his wife. 
Person1: The tuktuk took us to the tailors were a pushy seller persuaded us to buy some clothes of "very good quality". 
Person1: As soon as we paid the tuktuk took us to the next tourist attraction but on the way we read the reviews on Google maps and we realised that we were scammed.
Person1: The reviewers were saying that once they ordered the clothes they were never sent to their country as promised or the finishing was very bad, definitely not worth the money.
Person2: Oh shit!! And you already paid!!!!
Person1: Yeah. We felt horrible!!
Person1: We asked the driver to take us back but he refused. Of course, he already got his commission.
Person1: We ran back to the tailors. Fortunately it wasn't far. Within 10 minutes we were back. We told the pushy seller to cancel our order.
Person1: He said it was impossible because the fabric was already cut to our measurements. 
Person1: When we asked to see the cut fabric it was nowhere to be found, as it was already "sent to the factory". 
Person1: Then we said that we were going to call the police.
Person1: Only then he agreed to return us the money.
Person2: What a story!
Person2: I'm glad that you managed to get it back.
Person1: Yeah. It's like 1500 USD!
summary: Person1 got almost scammed in Bangkok at the tailor's, but luckily, having threatened the seller with police, she got her money back.

dialogue:
Person1: Hello Person2! A new update on our whereabouts. Just moved over to Merida after a long drive from Cancun. Empty roads giving you a weird feeling. We had all possible difficulties finding our airbnb accommodation as its address was like Marida, Caucel, Avenida 68, Puerta Sisal, Calle 31, Avenida Caucel 68, Calle 3/2419 B. After much asking around, as we don't have a navigation system here, and consulting our paltry maps, we gave up and phoned our host who navigated us to the house, which turned out to be located in a semi-fenced residential area outside the city. Quite a pretty and comfy place for that and entirely for us alone.
Person1: <file_photo>
Person1: So we finally had a goodnight's sleep, did some sightseeing in the capital of Yucatan today and are looking forward to reconnoiter the area tomorrow.
Person1: <file_photo>
Person2: Hi there! Many thanks for the details. Caucel rings a bell with me. Is it to the west of the city itself? A fairly new development?
Person1: That's it. Brand new and still being developed. Following a wide and brand new avenida today, we ended up with this. <file_photo> And dense vegetation beyond!
Person2: Looks like Mexico to me. But they'll pick up the continuation once they needed it. Practically minded as they are. And how did you like the city itself?
Person1: We got stuck on the Plaza Mayor, this being Sunday. It was turned into a market square with stalls offering local food, craftsmanship products and household goods, surprising un-touristy. In front of Palacio del Gobierno, a supreme show of dancing in local costumes.
Person1: <file_photo>
Person2: Did you manage to get to the balcony of the Palacio on the first floor and get some photos from there?
Person1: But of course!
Person1: <file_photo>
Person1: Theresa tried to prevent me from trespassing but you know me. Even managed to get to the loo there!
Person2: Good boy! And how about the cathedral? Casa de Montejo? Is it still accessible or is it only a bank?
Person1: Both, and Theresa intends to visit the cathedral again to take some more photos. I didn't find it that impressive, apart from the west facade of course. A small part of Casa de Montejo on the ground floor is a museum now, interiors with period furniture plus a small modern art gallery, quite pleasant though over-airconditioned, but the rest is a bank, I think.
Person2: If I remember correctly they bought the building some time ago and financed its restoration. To have a good overview of the city, you should try a ride on an open double-decker bus.
Person1: Planned for a day to come. Tomorrow we want to go to Sisal and drive along the coast to Progresso.
Person2: You'd better stay in Sisal, enjoy the beach and absolutely try one of their fish restaurants. As far as I remember the road leading eastwards peters out after a few kms and you are nowhere.  Years back with my team we mapped the ruins of Xcopte temple east of the road but it took us a strenuous march and even worse kayaking. I don't think it's been made open to sightseeing. I'd give it a miss anyway, nothing spectacular.

Person2: Absolutely! It is a must. Huge, well preserved, with a totally unique - oval - pyramid, el Piramide del Adivino. Plan one whole day for this site. It is exceptional. One of my favourites in this part of Yucatan.

Person2: I bet you are! Anyway please keep me posted about your travelling there.
Person1: Sure. Your tips are invaluable to us. You'll hear from us soon!
summary: Person1 and Theresa have just moved to Merida. They had problems getting there. They like their accommodation and they enjoy their sightseeing in the capital of Yukatan. They are planning to go to Sisal and Uxmal.

dialogue:
Person1: Hey! I need a little bit of your help. :D I was in Hamburg for almost 5 months and I wanted to post a short text for all my friends and peoplewho made me feel better in a new place. It will be public so I dont want to make grammar or vocabulary mistakes :P I'd be thankful if you saw it and improve it as a native speaker :)

Person2: How are you btw?
Person1: Its time to say good bye! During my Hamburg experience I had fun, I worked hard and I took a lot of walks in the harbour. I also realised that #Fischbrotchen and milkshake are not a perfect match. But most of all - I met incredible, inspiring and freindly people who gave me the best memories. Thanks for everyone, who made me smile! + special thanks for my sister who survived 5 months with me and my Netflix obsession.

Person1: I'm fine, tomorrow I'm leaving Germany ;) But i miss France actually :D What about you? Still studying in Bordeaux? ;)
Person2: Hey, I couldn't answer you straight away - here are my corrections:
Person2: It's time to say... It's = it is; Its = possessive form of it, meaning "of it". 2 examples  - 'The building was missing its windows.' and 'it's a lovely day outside!'
Person2: "Goodbye", not "good bye" ;)
Person2: This is such a petty thing for me to correct, but here goes - "During my Hamburg experience , I had fun..." (what can I say? Commas are important too :P )
Person2: I took a lot of walks *on* the harbour - just like you would say: "I took a walk on the beach" not "in the beach"
Person2: Milkshakes - plural (especially since you next write: milkshakes *are* not "is")
Person2: Thanks everyone who made me smile - the "for" isn't needed, if anything, "thanks to everyone" is preferred. And *a* special thanks *to* my sister - again, "to" not "for"

dialogue:
Person1: Hi, Person2, how's it going? Snowed in?
Person2: Yes, we bloody well are! The farm was cut off for a couple of days, awful, worst winter for a long time.
Person1: Yes, wasn't it? Did you manage to dig yourselves out?
Person2: Yes, eventually, they actually sent over some boys from the barracks down the road and a digger too! It took a few days, but it all got done.
Person1: Well, I haven't been in work for almost a week, the office was shut. Oh, and the supermarket shelves were almost empty, no deliveries were able to get through.
Person2: Wish that was the extent of my problems! I haven't been able to get fresh feed for the animals myself so, guess what? They helicoptered it in on Wednesday! They sent me and Dotty some food supplies too.
Person1: What about electricity etc?
Person2: Well, yeah, trouble with that and water for a day or two, then it was ok, but no fun sitting around with candles. We did have our log fire, though!
Person1: You managing to work now, animals ok?
Person2: Yes, so far, but we're going to be lambing soon, so hope the cold weather holds off, we really don't want to lose livestock.
Person1: Wonder how Gran and Grandpa managed in the old days, must have been hell.
Person2: Oh, yes indeed! Perhaps they stocked up just in case, rather than just being able to pop out in the jeep for supplies.
Person1: Yes, anyway, give my love to Dot! Keep in touch and keep warm!
Person2: Thanks cuz.
summary: Because of the snow Person1 didn't go to work for almost a week. Person2's farm was cut off for a couple of days until some boys with a digger helped them. They didn't have electricity, and the fresh feed for animals had to be helicoptered.

We plan on spending the night and coming back on Thursday since it’s a 4.5 hour drive. We will have 5 additional spots in the car if anyone wants to join. Please let us know ASAP in case we need to figure out shared accommodations! This natural event usually draws crowds so we need to move quickly.

Basically roughly once a month during nesting season, hundreds or thousands of sea turtles come to shore to make their nests and lay their eggs (called the arribada). It’s a natural phenomenon because somehow it’s inexplicably synchronized and they’re in a sort of trance over a 4-5 day period while they do this. Roughly 45-60 days later, the eggs hatch and the baby turtles run to shore. The last arribada was from Nov 2-7 which means they should hatch around the week of Dec 17.

dialogue:
Person1: What do you think of what's happening in the UK Parliament today?
Person2: You mean the resignations of four high-ranking ministers over the Brexit deal?
Person1: Yes.
Person2: Well, I don't think this deal is going to get signed. Apart from anything else it is worse than simply taking a second vote and hopefully being able to withdraw from Article 50 notice.
Person1: Can we even withdraw now?
Person2: Apparently we can do that. There are some opinions that say not, but in reality it would be a big relief to the other countries. 
Person2: The alternative, having no deal at all, is not only risky for the UK, but could cause big trouble to the rest of the states and of course there are quite big issues in the Eurozone already. This could tip over a very big landslide.
Person1: So you think we could get a better deal if we hold out?
Person2: Right now the optimal strategy would be to stay inside the EU, forget about leaving as we did not know the hurdles that would be placed by the powers that be. We need to work today with other Eurosceptic countries like Italy, Greece, Poland, Hungary and the other ex-Warsaw Pact countries.
Person1: To do what?
Person2: To change the EU into what we actually want it to be. To radically alter it so that it becomes what we hoped it was going to be.
Person1: Can that be done?
Person2: We see that the Germans have had enough of Merkel. When she goes, Macron also goes. It wouldn't take more than one of those bigger countries going the way of Italy, or a few more of the secondary states like Holland and Denmark, from the western side, to start a programme of deep change.
Person1: Makes sense. IN the end we all need to have some kind of co-operation in Europe.
Person2: Every Brexiteer I spoke to actually wants A European Union, they just don't want THIS European Union.
Person1: But is there any chance that there will be a second vote.
Person2: May has said no, but May could be finished in a week from now. If there is a General Election and all the Conservatives stand on a revote platform with UKIP and Labour saying no re-vote, then the Tories may well win. Then they would have to offer a re-vote.
Person1: What if we then end up staying in but other countries start defaulting and leaving us picking up the bills which was going to maybe happen to France and Germany?
Person2: That's the downside risk. Certainly if we are ever going to leave, the time to do it is now, or stay and fight for a different kind of Union which might not need countries to go crashing out of it that way. 
Person1: I don't know if you will every find a format that 30 countries will be able to agree on. 
Person2: Either you have to make it so that there is really not that much that they have to agree on, or you make everything so harmonised that it is really one country and everyone is unhappy with something. Where we are now is stuck in the middle, trying to agree and enforce too much, but still with options for countries to do things differently and to look after themselves. We haven't managed to deliver the European dream.
summary: Person2 would like Great Britain to stay in the European Union but according to him the EU should evolve. Person1 is sceptic if it's possible to find a solution on which 30 countries would agree.

dialogue:
Person1: Good evening Person2, I'd hate to bother you with a call at that unearthly time but I must ask you something that might be urgent but not before tomorrow morning. My sister had just taken a bad fall in the bathroom hitting her L lower rib cage against an edge of a bathtub and is experiencing general pain. She doesn't think she's broken anything. Would you think it might be something demanding medical attention?
Person2: Good evening Person1, I'm still in bed reading, Emma is asleep, so I'll stick to writing. Firstly, sorry to hear that but don't worry. If she can still move and talk, it can't be too bad. She doesn't spit blood, does she?

Person2: Is the impacted area swollen?
Person1: No.
Person2: BTW when did it happen?
Person1: Not more than an hour ago.

Person1: We couldn't talk because of my wife and the baby in the same room. She also preferred to write, since, as I suppose, it was less painful that talking. And yes – she was absolutely lucid.
Person2: Of course I cannot say anything definite without examining her but judging by the symptoms you've described I'd tend to say that it's just soreness due to the impact of the fall. But she has to observe her body.

Person2: If you're going to get them for her, take IBU-ratiopharm 400 g, 20 pills, and 10 pills of the same but 600 g. She may want to start with the stronger one.

Person2: Good night, Person1.
